claim_boundary: No AppBench task was executed, no application was generated or deployed, and no AppBench score was produced. This receipt reports data characterization, an immutable evaluation split manifest, a disjointness proof, and a primary-source license position. Nothing here is a model result.

execution_source.git_operations_performed: none (no commit, push, checkout, or branch change)

suite.substitution_note: No BrowserGym, Playwright, WebArena or other web-automation suite was used or proposed as an AppBench stand-in.

data_characterization.blob_match_method: local git blob sha1 recomputed and compared against the oid in https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/AfterQuery/App-Bench/tree/de80d5bcd404adee5307311571e512b5c37e6112
data_characterization.per_tool_score_columns_note: All nine per-tool columns are empty at the pinned revision (one cell holds a single space). The CSV contains no reference scores, so no gold-answer harness validation is possible from it.
data_characterization.rubric_items_match_note: AfterQuery states '151 rubric items (totaled across all 6 apps)'. The local parse yields exactly 151 (24/33/22/25/23/24), corroborating that the public CSV is the complete scored task set. AfterQuery makes no explicit 'this is the full set' statement.
data_characterization.what_a_task_specifies: A markdown Prompt (# Task / ## Functionality Overview / ## Feature Requirements numbered list), an identical per-task CLI addendum naming a Next.js template in an isolated Docker container with Supabase for auth and database, and a Rubric whose numbered items are 1:1 with the Feature Requirements. Verified: rubric item count equals requirement item count for all six tasks.
what_the_csv_does_not_specify: the Next.js starter template (contents, version, dependencies)
the Supabase project schema or provisioning
any wall-clock, token, or turn budget
the grading procedure (defined only in leaderboard prose, not in the data)

split_work.task_id_algorithm: sha256(canonical_json({content, dataset_id, revision, source_file, suite_id})) where canonical_json = json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True) and text is normalized CRLF/CR -> LF plus per-field strip
split_work.split_hash_matches_adapter_note: Asserted in test against pavlov_appbench_openreward_games_adapter._deterministic_split_hash, so the manifest drops straight into the E12 contract boundary.

disjointness.e13_note: E13 has no task IDs in this checkout, so the adapter's E12/E13 cross-boundary rule is not yet exercised against real E13 IDs.

heldout_status.held_out_reason: The source is the public 'vExternal' CSV published on the Hugging Face Hub on 2025-12-10, ungated, with a nonzero public download count (85 at probe time). Publication predates evaluation, so contamination cannot be excluded for any model whose training corpus postdates that date. No private held-out partition is published or mentioned by AfterQuery anywhere that primary-source search reached.
heldout_status.conclusion: The mechanical half of HELDOUT_TASK_SPLIT_UNPROVEN is closed. The contamination half cannot be closed from public artifacts and must not be asserted.

hugging_face.community_tab: one thread only: '[bot] Conversion to Parquet' by parquet-converter; no license discussion

corroborating_signal.observation: AfterQuery does declare licenses on other datasets it publishes, so the absence here is specific rather than an org-wide omission.

afterquery_site.scope_clause_verbatim: These Terms of Service govern your access to and use of AfterQuery's website and services.
afterquery_site.ip_clause_verbatim: The service and its original content, features, and functionality are owned by AfterQuery and are protected by international copyright, trademark, patent, trade secret, and other intellectual property laws.
afterquery_site.grant_to_users: none - the clause reserves rights and grants nothing; it does not address downloading, redistributing, or reusing published benchmark data

license_position.practical_position: AfterQuery has published no license and no terms grant covering App-Bench task data. Default copyright applies and there is no grant of use. This is a policy decision for the user, not a technical one. The unblock is a written permission or license from founders@afterquery.com.
license_position.action_required_by_user: Email founders@afterquery.com requesting a license or written permission for evaluation use of AfterQuery/App-Bench, or accept the risk explicitly in writing. This lane will not run scored evaluation until one of those exists.

official_harness_search.unrelated_runners_checked: AfterQuery/anvil is a SWE-bench-Pro runner; AfterQuery/harbor is a Terminal-Bench 2.0 fork; AfterQuery/FullStackBoilerplate is a hiring take-home, not the AppBench template. None references App-Bench.
official_harness_search.paper: none - the leaderboard 'Read paper' link points at appbench.ai (a website); arXiv returns no App-Bench result

unpublished_prerequisites: the pre-initialized Next.js starter template referenced by every task
per-tool trajectories and per-item scores (CSV score columns are empty)
any wall-clock, token, or turn budget

official_grading_protocol.detail: Two experienced full-stack developers graded each trajectory independently; contradicting grades were re-evaluated jointly to consensus. Graders exercised every rubric feature on the deployed app, verified database persistence, and tested multi-user flows.
official_grading_protocol.scoring: binary 1/0 per rubric item, no partial credit, summed across all 6 apps
official_grading_protocol.metric: total points earned / total possible points across all tasks (labelled 'Percentile' on the leaderboard, but computed as a percentage)
official_grading_protocol.attempts: 3 per task, one-shot each, best run scored; no interactive debugging or fix probes
official_grading_protocol.environment: isolated Docker container with Node.js, pre-initialized Next.js template, Supabase URL and keys provided; web builders got no template and deployed on their own cloud
official_grading_protocol.human_intervention: supplying API keys and service credentials on request only

native_runner_status.reproducibility_consequence: Because the official verifier is two human graders, any automated or LLM-judge verifier built locally is a different measurement. Its output must be labelled harness_validation with is_model_score false and must never be reported as an AppBench score or compared to the published leaderboard.

adapter_change.defect_found: _validate_source matched the marker 'appbench' as a raw lowercase substring, so the real upstream identifiers ('AfterQuery/App-Bench', 'app-bench') were rejected and no receipt could cite the authoritative source URL verbatim.
adapter_change.fix: Added _fold_source: lowercase and drop non-alphanumerics before matching both the required marker and the banned substitution markers.
adapter_change.safety: The change strengthens the substitution ban rather than loosening it - 'x-LAM' and 'related_benchmark' now fold onto their banned forms and are rejected. Two tests were added covering both directions.
adapter_change.blast_radius: zero external importers; every other flagship adapter defines its own private _validate_source
adapter_change.e13_scope: E13's required marker, evaluation role, and boundary semantics are unchanged.

fail_closed_assertion.asserts: the real E12 boundary, built from the real task IDs and split hash, is still rejected by the contract adapter because the license receipt and native contract are absent

cost.cost_to_cross_the_boundary_usd_estimate: unpriced - requires an agent model credential plus 6 tasks x 3 attempts x N tools of full-stack app generation with live third-party APIs; no credential is present in this environment

blockers.detail: AfterQuery publishes no license and no terms grant for App-Bench. Verified 2026-08-09: the HF dataset has no cardData key, no license tag, no README/LICENSE/NOTICE/TERMS at the pinned revision, and an empty dataset card; the leaderboard HTML contains zero occurrences of 'license'; the site ToS reserves rights over AfterQuery content and grants users nothing. The absence is specific - AfterQuery licenses three of its other six public datasets.
blockers.external_receipt_needed: written license or permission from founders@afterquery.com, or an explicit written risk acceptance by the user

blockers.detail: No AppBench task runner, deployment harness, artifact verifier, or side-effect verifier exists locally, and none is published upstream. The only App-Bench repo AfterQuery publishes is a 3-file documentation repo with no code. Three prerequisites (Next.js template, Supabase project, human graders) have no upstream artifact to pin against. A specification is now written at outputs/e12_appbench/native_runner_spec.md; it is a spec, not an implementation.
blockers.external_receipt_needed: none - this is buildable work, but steps 1-3 of the spec are unbuilt and step 4 needs an agent model credential
blockers.who_can_unblock: engineering time, plus an agent model key for the generation step

blockers.detail: The official AppBench verifier is two experienced full-stack developers grading each deployed app by hand against the rubric, with joint re-adjudication of disagreements. Any automated or LLM-judge verifier built locally measures something else. This blocker does not prevent building a harness; it prevents calling the harness output an AppBench score.
blockers.external_receipt_needed: two qualified human graders following the published dual-grading protocol, or an explicit downgrade of the claim to harness_validation

blockers.detail: Resolved: immutable content-addressed task IDs, a deterministic split hash byte-compatible with the contract adapter, an aggregate manifest hash, and a disjointness proof against 900 foreign task IDs across 41 files, all unit-tested (30 tests). Still open: the tasks are public on the Hugging Face Hub since 2025-12-10, so freedom from training contamination cannot be proven and is recorded as null, not true. Upstream publishes no private held-out partition.
blockers.external_receipt_needed: a private held-out partition from AfterQuery, or a model whose training cutoff provably predates 2025-12-10

blockers.detail: No W&B, Tinker, or Hugging Face checkpoint receipts exist because no experiment was attempted. Consistent with the cost boundary for this sprint.
